conventions.convention: Full AC; finite horizon T ≥ 0; finite positive state and noise dimensions; complete probability space and usual filtration; Brownian increments independent of the earlier filtration; an F₀-measurable square-integrable initial value independent of future Brownian increments.
Coefficients are jointly Borel, uniformly globally Lipschitz in state, and satisfy |b(t,x)| + ‖σ(t,x)‖F ≤ K(1 + |x|). Matrix stochastic integration means finite sums of scalar coordinate integrals.

A strong solution initially requires local coefficient integrability, adapted continuous paths and the integral identity on one measurable probability-one event; it does not assume a moment bound. Null-path replacements use F₀-measurable null sets. Uniqueness means indistinguishability.
For real p ≥ 2, the higher-moment theorem bounds sup over t of E|Xₜ|ᵖ, assuming E|X₀|ᵖ < ∞; it does not assert E sup over t of |Xₜ|ᵖ for p > 2.
A Lebesgue density is a nonnegative Lebesgue-measurable function representing the law on every Borel set. The singular-law example concerns the initial endpoint t = 0.

load_bearing.statement: A strong solution on [0,T] is an adapted continuous process satisfying the displayed finite-coordinate integral equation indistinguishably, with almost surely finite drift variation and diffusion energy, under the stated usual-filtration, initial-value, global Lipschitz and linear-growth hypotheses. No moment bound is included in the definition.

Under def-ito-sde-and-strong-solution on [0,T], there is a strong solution on the given filtered space, unique up to indistinguishability among strong solutions with the same initial value and Brownian driver, satisfying E sup₀≤t≤T |Xₜ|² ≤ (1 + 3E|X₀|²) exp((6K²T + 24mK²)T).

The Picard map Φ maps adapted continuous processes with finite expected squared path supremum into the same class. Its growth estimate has constant 6K²T + 24mK², its path-sup difference estimate has constant 2TL² + 8mL², and its constant-input first-iterate bound is (4K²T² + 16mK²T)(1 + E|X₀|²).

Under the coefficient and initial-value hypotheses of def-ito-sde-and-strong-solution on a finite horizon, every adapted continuous solution with locally defined drift and diffusion integrals satisfies E sup₀≤t≤T |Yₜ|² < ∞.
For every real p ≥ 2 with E|X₀|ᵖ < ∞, the unique solution satisfies sup₀≤t≤T E|Xₜ|ᵖ ≤ 2^(p/2)(1 + E|X₀|ᵖ) exp(CₚT), where Cₚ = √2 pK + p(p−1)K².

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier statement against the Girsanov, ULA pathwise KL and diffusion-density consumers. Their globally Lipschitz additive-noise equations have linear growth and square-integrable or deterministic initial values on usual Brownian spaces. They use strong existence, uniqueness and second path moments faithfully; density, reversibility and change of measure are established separately.

This is a background page prerequisite rather than a direct invocation of an owned theorem by the listed Euler–Maruyama items. The recursion explicitly adds a half-Hölder time modulus; its squared growth bound implies the supplier's linear-growth bound after a constant adjustment. The page keeps numerical pointwise moment estimates separate from exact-solution path-supremum bounds and asserts no convergence rate or density regularity.
